title: Principles six to nine
hook: prophecy, Moses' unique prophecy, the Torah from heaven, and its permanence

segments.voice: Yesterday, principles one to five, the foundations about God, and your line: one, bodiless, eternal. Did you let one too-small picture go? Today, the list's second stretch. Day one thousand one hundred thirty-five.

Two verses from the Torah. One: "Hear, O Israel: the LORD our God, the LORD is one." The other is from a list of names in Genesis: the sons of Ham were Cush, and Mizraim, and Put, and Canaan. One you met yesterday, at the heart of Jewish prayer. The other is easy to skim. Is one of them holier than the other? Maimonides gives a blunt answer, and it sits at the center of today's four foundations: the ones about prophecy, and about the Torah itself.
screen: `HEAR, O ISRAEL.` → `THE SONS OF HAM.` → `IS ONE HOLIER?`

segments.voice: Principles six to nine. The sixth: prophecy is real. God can speak to human beings, and some people, prepared and open, have heard. The seventh: the prophecy of Moses stands apart from every other. The Torah itself says so. In Numbers, God says that with other prophets He speaks in visions and dreams, but with Moses mouth to mouth, plainly, not in riddles. And at the end of Deuteronomy: no prophet has arisen since in Israel like Moses, whom the LORD knew face to face. That's why the line from last week's saying, from Moses to Moses, carried such weight. The eighth: the Torah is from heaven. The whole Torah we have, Maimonides says, is the one given to Moses. And here is his blunt answer to the two verses. There is no difference, he says, between the sons of Ham and Hear, O Israel. Both come from the same source. Holiness isn't measured by how moving a verse sounds. The ninth: the Torah won't be replaced. Nothing will be added to it, and nothing taken away. Deuteronomy says it directly: "thou shalt not add thereto, nor diminish from it." Put the four together and you get a chain. God speaks. Moses hears most clearly. What he receives is the Torah. And the Torah stays. Jews today hold the eighth and ninth in different ways, and that difference gets a day of its own soon. Prophecy and Torah.
screen: `GOD SPEAKS TO PEOPLE.` · `MOSES, MOUTH TO MOUTH.` · `EVERY VERSE FROM THE SAME SOURCE.` · `NOTHING ADDED, NOTHING TAKEN AWAY.` · then, large: `PROPHECY AND TORAH.`

segments.voice: Today's practice is to reflect on where Torah comes from, or on where any text you treasure comes from. Settle, and let your breath slow. Bring to mind the words that guide you most, from scripture, from a parent, from a teacher. Ask quietly: where did these reach me from? Who handed them on? Follow the chain back as far as you can, one link at a time, without forcing an answer. Then set the question down, and stay with the breath. The bell holds the time.
Principles six to nine. Prophecy is real, Moses' prophecy stands apart, the Torah is from heaven, and the Torah will not be replaced. Today's word.

Your line: prophecy and Torah. Today, read one plain, skippable line of something you treasure, a name, a list, a date, and give it the same attention as the famous lines. Day one thousand one hundred thirty-five.

howItsDone: The Torah is read aloud from a handwritten scroll in the synagogue on Shabbat, Mondays, Thursdays and festivals, and read through in order, over a yearly cycle or, in some communities, a longer one.
